sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE BHAGWATI PRASAD SHARMA

ON THE 7 th OF AUGUST, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 693 of 2009  THE NEW INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LTD  Versus  GOVIND PRASAD KUSHWAHA AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Dinesh Kaushal - Advocate for appellant/Insurance Co.
 None for respondents.
 ORDER

The present appeal has been filed by the appellant Insurance Company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, challenging the award dated 24.11.2008 passed by Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal in Claim Case No.942/2008.
2.

entities.text: Addl. Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that the appellants are parents of deceased Naveen who died in accident on 12/5/05 while his motor cycle in which he was going to his house dashed by offending Scorpio due to rash and negligent driving by its driver resulting in his death on 13/12/05 in Hamidiya hospital.

The appellants had filed claim petition before Claims Tribunal, Bhopal claiming compensation for death of their son stating that deceased was aged about 14 years and student of 10 class earning 3000/- p.m. by doing job of tailoring.
The respondent No. 3 and 4, owner and driver respectively denied the claim of the claimants and factum of accident.

The respondents denied its l i a b i l i t y o n t h e g r o u n d t h a t d r i v e r w a s n o t h a v i n g N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-JBP:37681 2 MA-693-2009 effective valid driving license and it was being driven in violation of terms and condition of policy.

The Tribunal after recording the evidence adduced by the claimants as well appellant held that offending vehicle was being driven in violation of terms and condition of the policy as the driver was not having valid effective driving license on the date accident, awarded compensation of sum of Rs 3,38,000/ against the respondents jointly and severally with liberty to recover from the owner and driver of the vehicle.
Hence this appeal has been filed.

3. The appellant Company had filed reply to the applications stating that the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective licence at the time of accident and as such the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of the policy.

The accident has been caused because of The New India Insurance Company Ltd vs Govind Prasad Kushwaha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12873144/
1 negligence of the deceased and accordingly prayed for dismissal of the application under section 166 of the Act of 1988.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of rival pleadings and evidence adduced by the parties, the learned Tribunal has allowed the application by granting compensation to the tune of Rs. 3, 38,000/- to the claimants along with interest @ 6 % per annum from the date of filing of application.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the present appeal is filed only on the ground of breach of policy as the offending vehicle was being plied in breach of the policy.
It has been submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not at all possessing the driving licence as has come on record through the evidence of the parties.

It is submitted that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37681 3 MA-693-2009 Singh and others, reported in 2004 ACJ 1 in para- 100 though issued the order with regard to pay and recover, but, at the same time, has observed that such order shall not be applied as a precedence in other cases where driver of the offending vehicle does not have licence at all and accordingly, prayed that direction issued by the Tribunal in regard to pay and recover is against the settled principles of law as laid down by the Apex Court.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Swaran NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37681 3 MA-693-2009
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No other ground has been raised by the appellant during the course of arguments.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

Recently, the Hon'ble Apex Court vide order dated 29.1.2025 in the case of M.Ananthi Vs.
P.Venkatesan and another passed in S.L.A (C) No.377/2023 has ordered pay and recover in the cases, where the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the said case on the factual background that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having licence and the lower court found that the Insurance Company cannot be held liable to compensate on account of such breach, the High Court did not order to pay the compensation first and recover it from the driver and owner, has allowed pay and recovery.

The Hon'ble Apex Court while allowing the prayer, modified the impugned judgment of the said case by directing the Insurance Company to pay compensation to the claimants first and then recover from the driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
8. On perusal of the record, it is found that the present case is akin to the case decided by Hon'ble Apex court in the case of M.Ananthi (supra) .

Thus, this Court is of the opinion that in the present case also the same NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:37681 4 MA-693-2009 direction which has been issued by the Tribunal against the Insurance Company for making payment of compensation first and then recover from the driver and owner is just and proper and cannot be faulted with and thus the same is hereby affirmed.
9.
With the aforesaid, the appeal is disposed of.
No order as to cost.
(BHAGWATI PRASAD SHARMA) JUDGE PG The New India Insurance Company Ltd vs Govind Prasad Kushwaha on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12873144/
